title: Zhu Rongji: A Reformer Who Centralized More Power in the Chinese State - The Wire China
gist: At a pivotal 1993 meeting ahead of China's fiscal centralization, then-vice premier Zhu Rongji told provincial officials the market economy must be constrained by law and administrative discipline rather than run by local officials' discretion — the article's title frames Zhu's reform legacy as one that ultimately centralized state power.

insights.claim: In 1993, ahead of China's fiscal centralization reforms, then-vice premier Zhu Rongji told provincial officials that the market economy is 'one of order and legality' and 'not whatever one wishes it to be,' explicitly rejecting the idea that local officials in charge of an area could act as they pleased.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Documents the ideological basis Beijing used to justify stripping fiscal discretion from provincial officials in the 1993-94 tax-sharing reform, a precedent relevant to understanding recurring central-versus-local fiscal power struggles in China today.
insights.quote: the market economy is one of order and legality. It is not whatever one wishes it to be, and it definitely is not one where an official in charge of an area can do as he wishes.

insights.claim: Zhu Rongji argued the market economy must be constrained by law, regulations, and administrative discipline and be subject to supervision by the party, framing market liberalization as compatible with, and dependent on, centralized party oversight.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Establishes an early articulation of the 'rule-bound but party-supervised market' model that continues to underpin how Beijing frames its economic reforms as compatible with continued party control — useful context for interpreting current regulatory crackdowns as consistent with, not a departure from, this doctrine.
insights.quote: The market economy must be constrained by the law, regulations, and administrative discipline and be subject to supervision by the part
insights.locator: stated “the market economy is one of order and legality”
